title: Tennis ball falling at 5 m s⁻¹
caption: At 5 m s⁻¹ the drag on a 0.06 kg tennis ball is 0.025 N against a weight of 0.59 N: a ratio of about 4%. Neglecting air resistance is a controlled approximation here, fine for a rough model.
alt: Free-body diagram of a falling tennis ball: weight 0.59 N down and drag 0.025 N up.
description: The ball is shown as a box. Its weight, mg = 0.06 × 9.81 = 0.59 N, acts straight down.
Drag acts upward, against the motion: ½ρC_dAv² = ½ × 1.2 × 0.5 × 0.0034 × 5² = 0.025 N, drawn to the same scale.
Drag ÷ weight = 4.3%; the net force is 0.56 N downward.
notes: drag ÷ weight ≈ 4%: neglect it for a rough model
